memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The son of Pallu was Eliab, and the sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan and Abiram. The same Dathan and Abiram were the community officials who rebelled against Moses and Aaron and were among Korah's followers when they rebelled against the LORD. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, whose followers died when the fire devoured the 250 men. And they served as a warning sign. But the line of Korah did not die out. - Num 26:8-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the midst of the census, the text pauses to recall a solemn event. Dathan, Abiram, and Korah had rebelled against the Lord, and the ground opened to swallow them while fire consumed their followers. Their judgment "served as a warning sign" for all who would come after. The census here becomes a moment of sober remembrance.

We should not skip over the seriousness of this. Rebellion against God is no light matter, and Scripture keeps the memory alive so that later generations would take heed. God's judgments are recorded not to frighten us needlessly but to teach us reverence and the danger of a proud, rebellious heart.

Yet notice the striking words at the end: "the line of Korah did not die out." Even after Korah's terrible rebellion, his descendants survived. And remarkably, some of them later became worship leaders in Israel; several psalms are attributed to the sons of Korah. Where there was judgment, God also wove in mercy and redemption.

This is the wonder of God's grace. He judges sin truly, yet He can bring good even from a family marked by rebellion. In Christ, no heritage of failure need define us, for God delights to redeem what seems lost (Rom 5:20). The same grace that spared Korah's line offers hope to all who come to God, whatever their past.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does God's judgment of rebellion teach you reverence?
2. What hope do you find in the survival of Korah's line?
3. How does God's grace redeem even a heritage of failure?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to take rebellion against You seriously, yet thank You that Your grace redeems even what seems lost. Let no failure of the past define me, for I am made new in Christ. Amen.
